newsitem.title: UK: U.S. world's largest dairy market, but growth lags.
newsitem.headline: U.S. world's largest dairy market, but growth lags.

text.p: The U.S. remains the world's largest market for dairy products, but Canada posted the most robust growth out of eight major markets, according to a study released on Monday.

With the exception of Canada, all the markets surveyed experienced sluggish growth in 1995, due to the mature nature of the worldwide dairy products market, Euromonitor, a market research group, said.
Canada and Italy were the only markets to post growth in real monetary terms, with Canada up 9.8 percent in 1995 and Italy up 1.3 percent.

The U.S., Germany, France and Spain all posted increases in volume, but in monetary terms they all saw declines in the value of their dairy markets, reflecting intense competition and consumer desire for value-oriented purchaes, Euromonitor said. The survey also include the UK and Japan.

The U.S. market, at $28.97 billion in 1995, was almost double the size of Germany, the second-largest dairy market at $15.18 billion. In volume terms, the U.S. also dwarfs Germany at 27.8 million tonnes, compared to 5.9 million tonnes in Germany for 1995.
But in the five years from 1991 to 1995 consumption of dairy products fell slightly in the U.S. to 27.8 million tonnes from 27.9 million.
Cheese is the principal dairy product in France, Italy, Germany and Canada, while milk dominates in the U.S., the UK and Spain, Euromonitor said.

In addition, the U.S. is the largest market for ice cream, yoghurt and chilled desserts, with the market valued at $10.9 billion in 1995. France is the second largest market for these products at $7.3 billion in 1995.

Americans consumed an average of 7.95 kilograms of ice cream in 1995, while the French were the largest yoghurt and chilled dessert consumers, eating an average of 20.79 kilograms of yoghurt and 11.48 kilograms of chilled desserts in 1995, Euromonitor said.
